good_patterns.title: Event listing uses bulk decoration rather than per-event queries
good_patterns.detail: Visibility membership and organizer, supervisor, and task counts are fetched in bounded bulk queries and grouped in Python. Preserve this shape when adding event summary fields; it avoids an obvious N+1 at the chapter's expected event counts.

good_patterns.title: Standing and scoring share a bulk engagement aggregate
good_patterns.detail: Members, required events, attendance, excuses, and fine invoices are each read once and grouped in memory. This is a good domain seam and should not be replaced with per-member service calls.

good_patterns.title: Modern financial mutations keep money, ledger, and audit writes inside RPCs
good_patterns.detail: The core monetary mutation is atomic, integer-cents, tenant-checked, and auditable. The defect is the Python work after the RPC, not the RPC boundary itself.

good_patterns.title: Frontend money formatting and input conversion are centralized
good_patterns.detail: The apparently separate dues, transaction, and balance helpers reuse one formatter and one string-based dollars-to-cents conversion. Their separation reflects different workflows rather than duplicated arithmetic.

good_patterns.title: Unimplemented AI-facing features return explicit non-results
good_patterns.detail: Bylaws Q&A returns `not_implemented`, while NL commands store no proposed actions and execute nothing. Preserve this honesty; do not replace it with fabricated answers or heuristic actions.

weird_but_reasonable.title: Router include order is intentionally load-bearing
weird_but_reasonable.detail: FastAPI path matching makes literal routes compete with `/{id}` routes. The append-order comments are justified, though route-order behavior should have focused tests rather than relying only on comments.

weird_but_reasonable.title: The RPC array-parameter registry works around psycopg2 function resolution
weird_but_reasonable.detail: The single-entry registry looks suspicious, but the comment accurately explains why a UUID-array parameter needs an untyped array literal while JSONB lists must remain JSON. Preserve the workaround until RPC invocation uses explicit parameter casts or typed SQL.

weird_but_reasonable.title: Three events notification files have distinct responsibilities despite confusing names
weird_but_reasonable.detail: This is not three duplicate implementations: one is transport routing, one enqueues lifecycle emails, and one implements event SMS completeness/dispatch. Renaming them to `notify_routes.py`, `email_notifications.py`, and `sms_notifications.py` would clarify the distinction without collapsing valid boundaries.

weird_but_reasonable.title: `fines_legacy` is a compatibility URL adapter over the current invoice model
weird_but_reasonable.detail: The filename is misleading, but retaining `/api/fines` while translating `unpaid_invoices(kind='fine')` into the old frontend shape is reasonable during migration. Remove it only with a versioned client/API transition.

weird_but_reasonable.title: `unpaid_invoices` is historically named but functions as the invoice aggregate
weird_but_reasonable.detail: The table contains partially paid, paid, and cancelled invoices, so its name is inaccurate. Renaming a heavily referenced financial table is higher risk than documenting it as the invoice aggregate and changing only through a planned migration.

conventions.dominant: Python uses snake_case; RPCs use domain prefixes (`tr_`, `ev_`, `at_`, `tk_`, `in_`, `an_`, `au_`, `rbac_`, `ch_`, `rc_`); permission keys are colon-delimited capabilities.
conventions.competing: The database client is universally called `sb` and documented as Supabase-shaped despite being psycopg2; current code carries names such as `fines_legacy`, `unpaid_invoices`, and `react-example`.
conventions.recommendation: Officialize RPC and permission naming. Rename local variables to `db` in new code and document historical schema/API names rather than propagating them into new symbols.

conventions.dominant: Large domains generally use `api/`, `services/`, `core/`, `auth.py`, and optional `notifications.py`; four multi-router domains use `api/router.py`.
conventions.competing: RBAC has `db/repositories`; auth and members omit much of the canonical shape; calendar, contribution, and instrumentation are read-side packages; tasks also exposes a separately mounted operations API; local untracked `db/__pycache__` directories make some packages appear to have a DB layer.
conventions.recommendation: Describe the layout as a menu of layers, not a mandatory shape. Reserve `db/repositories` for deliberately SQL-centric reads and remove stale generated directories outside this audit.

conventions.dominant: There are 346 absolute `api.*` import lines versus 15 relative import lines; platform and RBAC are common inward dependencies.
conventions.competing: Cross-domain imports include events→announcements/attendance, treasury→attendance, calendar→events/treasury/instrumentation, memberadmin→treasury, cron→auth/announcements/treasury, and chapters importing private `_client_ip` from auth.
conventions.recommendation: Make absolute imports official. Publish shared platform-level interfaces for client-IP parsing, notifications, and derived signals; prohibit imports of another domain's underscore-prefixed symbol.

conventions.dominant: Modern event/initiative routes translate named domain exceptions through context managers; the global handler provides opaque unexpected 500s.
conventions.competing: There are 43 actual broad `except Exception` handlers. They range from justified provider/telemetry containment (`cron/outbox_drain.py:271`, `instrumentation/services/usage.py:36`) to silent suppression (`platform/outbox.py:102,160`, `events/notifications.py:37,76`) and raw RPC-text translation (`tasks/api/*.py`, `treasury/api/*.py`). Raw `str(exc)` reaches clients in treasury reports/invoices/payments/fines, while string matching controls chapters and members errors.
conventions.recommendation: Adopt named domain errors and SQLSTATE/constraint-name mapping. Permit broad catches only at explicit best-effort/provider boundaries, with logging and a documented return contract.

conventions.dominant: Responses use snake_case DTOs and FastAPI's `{detail: ...}` error envelope.
conventions.competing: Only 9 `response_model=` declarations exist across 139 route decorators. Routes otherwise return raw RPC JSON, raw rows, bespoke dicts, lists, or Pydantic instances; `detail` alternates among strings, `{message, code}`, and `{message, counts/errors}` objects.
conventions.recommendation: Define response models for externally consumed routes first and standardize a typed error object while preserving FastAPI's outer `detail` field during migration.

conventions.dominant: Mutation bodies usually use domain-local Pydantic schemas and financial amounts are integer cents.
conventions.competing: Several filters and transitions accept bare strings: announcement/fine/task/outbox statuses, member role as a query argument, and generic method/status values that are validated only by SQL or error-string handling.
conventions.recommendation: Use Literal/Enum fields for closed vocabularies and constrained pagination parameters. Keep DB CHECK constraints as defense in depth.

conventions.dominant: Timestamps are intended to be timezone-aware ISO 8601; frontend `isoDay` deliberately preserves local calendar days.
conventions.competing: Event date/time are separate naive columns, multiple services independently coerce str/datetime values, and `_parse_ts` is duplicated in invoice presentation and member dashboard. The raw DB client returns Python date/time objects for reads but strings for writes.
conventions.recommendation: Centralize DB-to-API temporal serialization and timestamp parsing. Define chapter timezone semantics separately from absolute timestamps.

conventions.dominant: Database IDs are UUIDs and public schemas generally type them as strings.
conventions.competing: Raw SELECT returns `uuid.UUID`, writes/RPCs often return strings, so code inconsistently compares directly or wraps `str(...)`. The inconsistency appears throughout visibility sets, presenters, and member checks.
conventions.recommendation: Normalize all database result IDs to strings at the platform boundary or use UUID objects consistently in internal code and serialize only at HTTP boundaries.

conventions.dominant: DB CHECK constraints define per-aggregate lifecycle states.
conventions.competing: Invoice storage uses `unpaid/partially_paid/paid/cancelled`, V1 presentation uses `open/paid/void`, outbox uses `pending/sending/sent/failed/simulated`, and legacy task/event-task systems use unrelated task states. Mappings are distributed across services and frontend adapters.
conventions.recommendation: Keep per-aggregate enums, but define each once in a domain schema and one explicit API mapping; do not reuse generic `status: str` across aggregates.

conventions.dominant: Eight modules define loggers; global middleware attaches/returns a request ID and logs unhandled exceptions.
conventions.competing: Most modules have no logger, provider/outbox errors store exception strings in rows, and `current_request_id()` has zero callers. The log formatter does not inject the context variable into ordinary service records.
conventions.recommendation: Add a logging filter that includes the request context automatically and use structured fields for domain/target IDs. Remove or use `current_request_id`.

conventions.dominant: Collection routes commonly use a trailing slash and the frontend records exact mounted paths.
conventions.competing: Resource-specific endpoints mix slash and no-slash forms; correctness depends on registration order and `api.ts` warns that trailing slashes matter.
conventions.recommendation: Freeze existing public paths, but define one convention for new routes and add route-table contract tests before any normalization/redirect work.

conventions.dominant: Tests are domain-grouped, use descriptive function names, and important RPC/trigger tests hit PostgreSQL.
conventions.competing: Treasury retains implementation-sequence names such as `test_chunk0`, `test_chunkA`, and `test_chunkG`; route-registration tests can preserve obsolete surfaces without validating behavior.
conventions.recommendation: Name new tests by capability/invariant, gradually split chunk files, and require behavior coverage before treating route existence as a compatibility contract.

conventions.dominant: React module components generally default-export components, while hooks and pure helpers use named exports; API DTOs are centralized in `api.ts`.
conventions.competing: The actual layout is flat `components/*Module.tsx`, `hooks/`, `lib/`, `adapters.ts`, and `formatters.ts`, not the documented `app/components/modules/lib/contracts` architecture. `api.ts` is a 700+ line client/type registry.
conventions.recommendation: Officialize the current export split, then decompose `api.ts` by domain behind one shared request function rather than creating a second client layer.

conventions.dominant: Most modern services accept `sb` first and keyword-only business arguments.
conventions.competing: Older services call `get_db()` internally; attendance link/session code mixes both styles; several services are `async def` despite performing only synchronous DB work.
conventions.recommendation: Pass the DB/transaction context explicitly to services and keep them synchronous unless they actually await nonblocking work.

conventions.dominant: Runtime configuration is centralized in `Settings`; `.env.example` documents database, auth, messaging, email, and observability values.
conventions.competing: `PLATFORM_SECRET` and `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` are Settings fields but absent from `.env.example`. Local env names include ignored historical flags and Supabase/SendGrid variables not represented in Settings; `extra='ignore'` silently accepts them.
conventions.recommendation: Generate or test the env reference against Settings. Move ignored historical names to a documented legacy section or remove them from deployment configuration.

good_patterns.title: Money moves in one plpgsql transaction
good_patterns.detail: Invoice create, verify, void, refund, adjustment, expense, and bulk dues each insert the operational row, the big_ledger row, and the audit_logs row in one function body. The Python client autocommits every statement, so this is the only atomicity that exists. Do not split these back into service-layer inserts.

good_patterns.title: Double-verify is closed by a row lock plus a partial unique index
good_patterns.detail: Both verify RPCs SELECT the submission FOR UPDATE, return the existing verified payment when status is already approved, and rely on UNIQUE (submission_id) WHERE submission_id IS NOT NULL. Reject-after-approve raises. The idempotency row stores _created false so a replay does not notify twice. Keep that trio; the missing Idempotency-Key on the SPA verify call is safe only because of it.

good_patterns.title: Money is integer cents at the value object and in the treasury CHECKs
good_patterns.detail: Money rejects bool and float. Invoice, payment, allocation, expense, refund, and line-item amounts are BIGINT with CHECK (amount_cents > 0). Adjustments are signed BIGINT on purpose. dollarsToCents parses the digit string and never uses binary float. Leave this boundary alone; the NUMERIC leftovers are events.fine_amount, event_templates.default_fine_amount, fines.amount, and ev_create_event.p_fine_amount.

good_patterns.title: Refund cap and adjustment sign-off are enforced inside the RPC
good_patterns.detail: Active refunds against one verified payment cannot exceed that payment, under a FOR UPDATE on the payment. Over-threshold adjustments insert pending with no ledger row until a different officer approves. The threshold is real; the hole is everything under it, not the gate itself.

good_patterns.title: Per-file migration transactions and a fail-closed prod guard
good_patterns.detail: Each SQL file commits or rolls back as a whole, which is what makes a mid-file failure atomic. require_prod refuses while PROD_PROJECT_REFS is empty, and require_demo refuses anything that is not the demo ref or localhost. Keep the guard fail-closed. The hole is what happens after the set is filled, not the empty set.

weird_but_reasonable.title: Balances ignore big_ledger on purpose
weird_but_reasonable.detail: Chapter cash and member outstanding are derived from operational rows so a bad ledger entry cannot move money. Rebuild is a report, and apply_repairs rewrites only member_finance_accounts. That split is why ledger immutability is not the same thing as balance integrity, and it is the right shape as long as the operational amounts stay frozen.

weird_but_reasonable.title: Voiding a partially paid invoice forgives the whole face and leaves the payment as credit
weird_but_reasonable.detail: tr_void_invoice allows unpaid and partially_paid, writes status cancelled (there is no 'void' value), and posts CANCEL_INVOICE for the full face. It does not reverse allocations. BalanceEngine drops the invoice from owed and still counts the payment, so a $100 invoice with $40 paid goes from owing $60 to a $40 credit. The SQL comment says that is the decision. Paid invoices cannot be voided; the path for those is refund or adjustment. Do not 'simplify' this into deleting the payment.

weird_but_reasonable.title: login_attempts has RLS and zero policies
weird_but_reasonable.detail: The table has no chapter_id because failures are recorded for emails that match nobody. RLS with no policy is deny-all for every role that is not the owner. The app connects as the owner, so rate limiting still works. A future non-owner role would be unable to insert attempts and the limiter would fail open if that insert error is swallowed. idempotency_keys is the same shape (RLS on, no policy) and would break retries the same way.

weird_but_reasonable.title: PAYMENT_RECEIVED from 0012 uses the invoice as source_id
weird_but_reasonable.detail: The backfill had no submission, so the ledger row points at unpaid_invoices. The rebuild key that ignores source is the accommodation for that one shape. The accommodation is broader than the migration. Keep a special case for those rows; stop using it for every payment.

conventions.dominant: BIGINT cents on treasury tables, Money in Python, dollarsToCents string parse in greekos
conventions.competing: NUMERIC(10,2) on events.fine_amount, event_templates.default_fine_amount, and fines.amount; ev_create_event.p_fine_amount NUMERIC; FineToInvoice.fine_amount typed as float then str()'d; adapters.ts stores amount = amount_cents/100 beside amountCents
conventions.recommendation: Keep cents as the only stored and summed representation. Leave the NUMERIC columns frozen with the fines table. Stop dividing cents by 100 for anything that is later added.

conventions.dominant: DB CHECK unpaid | partially_paid | paid | cancelled. V1 HTTP maps unpaid/partially_paid to open and cancelled to void via present_invoice_v1
conventions.competing: Standing counts only unpaid fines. fine_summary treats partial as fully unpaid. adaptFines treats cancelled as Paid. tr_void writes cancelled, never void. Dashboard overdue_invoice_count counts every unpaid and partially_paid row, not due_at < now
conventions.recommendation: Pick remaining cents as the owed figure for every reader. Keep the four DB statuses. Map them at the edge once.

conventions.dominant: tr_verify_payment_v2 writes invoice_id NULL and payment_allocations; tr_refresh_invoice_status derives status
conventions.competing: tr_verify_payment and the 0012 backfill set verified_payments.invoice_id and write status from that column alone. tr_invoice_remaining_cents subtracts both
conventions.recommendation: One coverage path. Allocations are the one that can be reversed without rewriting history.

conventions.dominant: UNIQUE (chapter_id, operation, key) and the RPC returns the stored jsonb
conventions.competing: No payload hash; NULL keys are allowed and do not dedupe (fine_processor passes None); tr_cancel_invoice and tr_invalidate_expense accept p_idempotency_key and never read it; SPA verify sends no key
conventions.recommendation: Hash the canonical body into the key, or reject a replay whose body differs. Use the parameter in every RPC that declares it.

extra.title: invariant: treasury amounts are integer cents
extra.detail: Enforced: BIGINT + CHECK amount_cents > 0 on invoices, submissions, verified payments, allocations, line items, expenses, refunds. Adjustments are signed BIGINT with no zero check. Ledger amounts are signed BIGINT with no sign-vs-type check. Assumed: callers pass int cents. Bypass: events.fine_amount NUMERIC, fines.amount NUMERIC, event_templates.default_fine_amount NUMERIC, ev_create_event p_fine_amount NUMERIC, FineToInvoice.fine_amount: float then str(), postgres._serialize Decimal→float on RETURNING. Tests: money unit tests and treasury RPC tests. Strength: strong on the treasury tables, weak on the legacy NUMERIC columns.

extra.title: invariant: big_ledger and audit_logs are append-only
extra.detail: Enforced: big_ledger_no_delete, big_ledger_limited_update (active→invalidated only, other columns frozen), audit_logs_immutable. Same delete/update block on receipts, payment_allocations, payment_evidence, invoice_line_items. fines frozen entirely. Assumed: the owner will not DROP TRIGGER. Bypass: owner can disable triggers (accepted). The allowed status flip writes no audit_logs row. LedgerWriter.invalidate can do the flip and has no production caller. Strength: strong against ordinary SQL, absent against the owner.

extra.title: invariant: member outstanding = owed - paid + adjustments + refunds, cancelled excluded
extra.detail: Enforced in Python only, on read/recompute. owed sums non-cancelled invoice faces (paid invoices still count). paid sums every verified payment. refunds add (member owes again). chapter cash subtracts refunds. tr_void writes cancelled, so a voided invoice drops out of owed. Not enforced: no DB view. Bypass: UPDATE of the source amounts. Readers that do not recompute (dashboard, CSV, SMS) can disagree. Tests: chunk B/E/G. Strength: strong if the source rows are intact, partial across readers.

extra.title: invariant: one verified payment per submission
extra.detail: Enforced: partial UNIQUE (submission_id) WHERE NOT NULL, plus FOR UPDATE. Multiple NULL submission_ids are allowed so 0012 can insert historical payments. Reject of an approved submission raises. Tests: test_chunkC_payments.py, test_v1_allocation.py idempotent replay. Strength: strong.

extra.title: invariant: idempotency key returns the first result and does not cover a different body
extra.detail: Enforced: UNIQUE (chapter_id, operation, key). NULL keys do not collide. Not enforced: payload hash, expiry. tr_cancel_invoice and tr_invalidate_expense ignore the parameter. A reused key with a new dues-run body returns the old invoice ids; the service still recomputes the new member ids. Tests exist for same-key replay. Strength: partial.

extra.title: invariant: refunds cannot exceed the source payment
extra.detail: Enforced: FOR UPDATE on the payment, sum of active refunds + new amount <= payment amount, CHECK amount_cents > 0. Not enforced: reopening the invoice, actor != member. Status 'invalidated' is in the CHECK but no RPC sets it; an owner UPDATE to invalidated would drop the refund from the balance and leave the ledger row. Tests: test_chunkE_adjustments_refunds.py. Strength: strong for the cap, absent for undoing coverage.

extra.title: invariant: adjustments at or above $500 need a second officer
extra.detail: Enforced: pending with no ledger row until tr_approve_adjustment, which rejects approver = officer_id. Not enforced: actor != subject, a floor on repeated under-threshold calls, chapter-level vs member-level meaning (null member_id hits chapter cash only). Officer role holds the permission. Tests: test_chunkE sign-off cases. Strength: partial.

extra.title: invariant: invoice status matches coverage
extra.detail: Enforced for v2 and reallocate via tr_refresh_invoice_status (cancelled left alone; remaining <= 0 → paid; remaining < face → partially_paid). Bypassed by tr_verify_payment, which writes status from direct payments only and can overwrite cancelled. Reallocate of a payment that still has invoice_id double-counts. Tests cover v2 oldest-first, not the legacy writer. Strength: partial.

extra.title: invariant: a fine invoice is unique per event and member
extra.detail: Not enforced. The only partial unique on invoices is legacy_fine_id. issue_fines uses idempotency key fine:{event}:{member} inside tr_create_invoice_v2, so two concurrent calls with that same key cannot both commit. _already_fined_ids includes cancelled rows, so a waived fine cannot be reissued through that route, and a replay would return the original unpaid snapshot. process_event_fines passes p_idempotency_key None, so the race is open there. Strength: absent as a constraint, partial on the V1 route.

extra.title: invariant: member email is globally unique
extra.detail: Enforced: members.email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, not (chapter_id, email). One person cannot be in two chapters. Chapter self-signup collides with any existing member. Strength: strong as a constraint, and it is a product limit rather than a treasury bug.

extra.title: invariant: one attendance row and one excuse row per event and member
extra.detail: Enforced: attendance_unique_event_member and excuses_unique_event_member. checkin_links.short_code is UNIQUE. Attendance has no chapter_id in 0001; 0146 adds it via a derive trigger and enables RLS. Direct upsert from the check-in route and at_set_attendance both write the table. Strength: strong for the uniqueness, partial for which writer leaves an audit row.

extra.title: invariant: every financial RPC writes audit_logs
extra.detail: Create invoice (v1 and v2), bulk, verify (both), reject, void, cancel, expense create/invalidate, adjustment create/approve, refund, and reallocate all insert audit_logs. Reallocate and void reuse VERIFY_PAYMENT and CANCEL_INVOICE with metadata.op because the action CHECK is frozen. p_actor_id is nullable; fine_processor passes None, so those audit rows have a null actor. big_ledger has no actor column at all. Not every financial table change is an RPC: payment_evidence is a direct insert. Strength: strong for the RPC paths, absent for owner UPDATEs of operational amounts.

extra.title: invariant: tenant on money RPCs
extra.detail: Invoice, adjustment, bulk, and submit paths require the member (and the invoice) to sit in p_chapter_id. Verify locks the submission with chapter_id in the WHERE. Reallocate checks the payment and each target invoice. Not enforced by RLS at runtime (owner connection; helpers read request.jwt.claim.sub, which this client never sets). No FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on any table. Strength: strong inside the RPCs, absent at the table grant layer.

extra.title: table: chapters
extra.detail: Owner: chapters domain. No chapter_id (it is the root). No RLS. PK id. Written by ch_create_chapter (0156, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path=public). ON DELETE CASCADE from here fans into almost every tenant table and then hits append-only triggers, so a chapter delete fails once a ledger row exists.

extra.title: table: members
extra.detail: Owner: members/auth. chapter_id FK to chapters. No RLS. email globally UNIQUE. role CHECK officer|member, which is narrower than the RBAC catalog. password_hash nullable. Direct updates: sms consent, password via au_set_password, token_version, legacy role via mem_set_legacy_role. No DELETE route; FKs from invoices are ON DELETE CASCADE, so a raw delete would try to remove invoices and then fail on receipts/ledger.

extra.title: table: events
extra.detail: Owner: events. chapter_id FK. No RLS. fine_amount NUMERIC(10,2). linked_budget_id UUID with no FK (0090 TODO). Written by ev_create_event (0141, p_fine_amount NUMERIC) and direct updates (templates set fine_amount, linked session). Indexes on chapter_id, date, type, group, supervisor, visibility.

extra.title: table: attendance
extra.detail: Owner: attendance. UNIQUE (event_id, member_id). chapter_id added and RLS enabled in 0146 (select policy). Trigger at_derive_chapter_id. Written by at_set_attendance and by a direct upsert in api/attendance/api/attendance.py. Indexes on event_id, member_id, chapter_id.

extra.title: table: excuses
extra.detail: Owner: attendance. UNIQUE (event_id, member_id). RLS since 0146. Written by direct insert/delete in excuses.py and by at_set_attendance / at_review_excuse. Approve path voids one unpaid fine invoice.

extra.title: table: checkin_links
extra.detail: Owner: attendance. short_code UNIQUE. RLS since 0146. Direct insert and active=false updates in checkin_links.py. Index on short_code, event_id, chapter_id.

extra.title: table: fines
extra.detail: Owner: treasury legacy. chapter_id. No RLS. amount NUMERIC(10,2). Trigger fines_frozen blocks INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE via tr_block_all_mutation. No writer should touch it. 0012 copied rows into unpaid_invoices.

extra.title: table: event_templates
extra.detail: Owner: tasks legacy. chapter_id nullable for global templates. No RLS. default_fine_amount NUMERIC(10,2). Unique on global type. Seeded by the migration itself. Python templates service reads it and copies default_fine_amount onto events.fine_amount.

extra.title: table: event_template_roles
extra.detail: Owner: tasks legacy. No chapter_id, no RLS. FK to event_templates ON DELETE CASCADE. Index on template_id. No current RPC writer found; leftover of the operations engine.

extra.title: table: event_template_tasks
extra.detail: Owner: tasks legacy. No chapter_id, no RLS. FK to templates. Index on template_id.

extra.title: table: event_roles
extra.detail: Owner: tasks legacy. No chapter_id, no RLS. FK event_id CASCADE, member SET NULL. Indexes on event_id and assigned member.

extra.title: table: event_tasks
extra.detail: Owner: tasks legacy. No chapter_id, no RLS. Unique dedupe index. Direct insert from api/tasks/services/templates.py. Indexes on event_id and role_id.

extra.title: table: post_event_reports
extra.detail: Owner: tasks legacy. No chapter_id, no RLS. FK event_id CASCADE. Index on event_id. No treasury writer.

extra.title: table: treasury_grants_archived_0147
extra.detail: Created as treasury_grants. Unique (chapter_id, member_id, capability). RLS select policy. 0147 as corrected renames it and stops reading it; treasury_has_capability now reads the RBAC catalog. A demo that ran the first 0147 dropped the table instead. No runtime writer.

extra.title: table: idempotency_keys
extra.detail: Owner: platform/treasury. chapter_id FK. RLS enabled, zero policies (deny-all for non-owners). UNIQUE (chapter_id, operation, key). Written only inside money and other RPCs. result jsonb has no body hash. Index on chapter_id.

extra.title: table: big_ledger
extra.detail: Owner: treasury. chapter_id FK. RLS select via treasury_has_capability. Append-only triggers. entry_type CHECK includes the seven treasury types. source_id has no FK (polymorphic). member_id ON DELETE SET NULL. Indexes: chapter, member, (source_table, source_id), created_at. Written by every tr_* money RPC. LedgerWriter.insert/update exists and is test-only. No actor column.

extra.title: table: audit_logs
extra.detail: Owner: shared. chapter_id FK. RLS select. Append-only trigger. action CHECK widened over time (0152 adds UPDATE_TASK, CANCEL_TASK by rewriting the constraint). actor_id nullable ON DELETE SET NULL. Written by tr_*/ev_*/tk_* RPCs and by a direct insert in announcements outbox retry. Indexes: chapter, actor, (target_table, target_id), created_at.

extra.title: table: unpaid_invoices
extra.detail: Owner: treasury. chapter_id and member_id FKs CASCADE. source_event_id FK to events SET NULL. RLS select. CHECK kind (includes manual after 0120), amount_cents > 0, status unpaid|partially_paid|paid|cancelled. No immutability trigger. Unique only on legacy_fine_id. Indexes: chapter, member, status, partial source_event_id, partial due_at. Written by tr_create_invoice, tr_create_invoice_v2, tr_bulk_create_invoices, status updates from verify/void/cancel/refresh. No (member, source_event, kind) unique.

extra.title: table: payment_submissions
extra.detail: Owner: treasury. chapter_id, member_id FKs. invoice_id nullable since 0123. RLS. CHECK amount > 0, method includes check, status pending|approved|rejected. No update/delete trigger; status is updated inside verify/reject. Indexes: chapter, member, invoice, status, (chapter, status), method, created_at. Written by tr_submit_payment and tr_submit_balance_payment.

extra.title: table: verified_payments
extra.detail: Owner: treasury. chapter_id, member_id FKs CASCADE. invoice_id nullable since 0124. submission_id unique where not null, ON DELETE SET NULL. CHECK amount > 0. RLS select. No update/delete trigger. Indexes: chapter, member, invoice. Written only by tr_verify_payment, tr_verify_payment_v2, and the 0012 backfill. Balance reads amount_cents from here.

extra.title: table: member_finance_accounts
extra.detail: Owner: treasury cache. chapter_id FK. UNIQUE (member_id) not (chapter, member). RLS select. Columns are total_owed/paid/outstanding/current cents (the stage-1 inventory's balance_cents names are wrong). Written only by BalanceEngine.recompute_member upsert. Read without recompute by dashboard, CSV, SMS audience, announcement feed.

extra.title: table: receipts
extra.detail: Owner: treasury. chapter_id FK with no ON DELETE action. verified_payment_id UNIQUE. invoice_id nullable since 0124. CHECK amount > 0. Triggers block update and delete. RLS select. Written by both verify RPCs. Because the receipt cannot be deleted, the parent payment cannot be deleted either; its amount can still be updated.

extra.title: table: chapter_expenses
extra.detail: Owner: treasury. chapter_id FK. CHECK category, amount > 0, status active|invalidated. RLS select (treasury read only). No delete trigger. Index on chapter and status. Written by tr_create_expense and tr_invalidate_expense (the invalidate function accepts an idempotency key and does not read it). Chapter balance counts active rows only.

extra.title: table: finance_adjustments
extra.detail: Owner: treasury. chapter_id FK. member_id nullable (null means chapter-level). officer_id NOT NULL REFERENCES members ON DELETE SET NULL, which will fail the NOT NULL when that member is deleted. CHECK kind, non-empty reason, status pending|active. Delete trigger only. RLS. delta_cents signed, updatable. Written by tr_create_adjustment and tr_approve_adjustment. Indexes: chapter, member, status.

extra.title: table: refunds
extra.detail: Owner: treasury. chapter_id, member_id, verified_payment_id FKs. CHECK amount > 0, reason, status active|invalidated. Delete trigger only; no invalidate RPC despite the status value. RLS. Written by tr_issue_refund. Indexes: chapter, member, payment, status. Same officer_id NOT NULL ON DELETE SET NULL footgun.

extra.title: table: message_outbox
extra.detail: Owner: announcements/cron. chapter_id. No RLS. Unique dedup_key. Indexes: chapter, status, (target_table, target_id), partial (created_at) WHERE status=pending. No (status, channel, created_at) index; channel was added in 0159. Direct insert from platform/outbox.py and status updates from the drain. Trigger outbox_pin_sms_channel.

extra.title: table: roles
extra.detail: Owner: rbac. Global catalog, no chapter_id. RLS select-all. PK key. Seeded by migrations. No per-request writer.

extra.title: table: permissions
extra.detail: Owner: rbac. Global, no chapter_id. RLS select-all. PK key. Seeded by 0083/0121/0147. No runtime writer.

extra.title: table: role_permissions
extra.detail: Owner: rbac. No chapter_id. PK (role_key, permission_key). RLS select-all. Index on permission_key. Written by migration seeds, not by a request path.

extra.title: table: member_roles
extra.detail: Owner: rbac. chapter_id FK. UNIQUE (member_id, role_key, chapter_id). RLS select by rbac_request_chapter_id (JWT GUC, unset at runtime). Indexes: chapter, member, role_key. Written by rbac_assign_role / rbac_revoke_role and the 0147 backfill.

extra.title: table: attendance_sessions
extra.detail: Owner: attendance. chapter_id. RLS select. Indexes on chapter, event, created_at. Linked from events.linked_attendance_session_id.

extra.title: table: task_groups
extra.detail: Owner: tasks. chapter_id. RLS select. Index on chapter and event_id. Written alongside tk_* task RPCs.

extra.title: table: tasks
extra.detail: Owner: tasks. chapter_id. RLS. Indexes: chapter, group, assignee, status, due_at, event_id, initiative_id, partial security. Written by tk_create_task, tk_update_task, tk_update_task_status, tk_cancel_task, tk_commit_task and the direct people_needed update in tasks.py.

extra.title: table: announcements
extra.detail: Owner: announcements. chapter_id. RLS. Indexes: chapter, status, created_at, partial calendar. Written by an_send_announcement and direct delete/hide updates. Calendar columns added in 0152.

extra.title: table: recruits
extra.detail: Owner: recruitment. chapter_id. RLS. Indexes: chapter, stage, created_at. Written by rc_update_recruit_stage and recruitment services. Phone rewritten by 0149.

extra.title: table: bylaws_documents
extra.detail: Owner: bylaws. chapter_id. RLS. Indexes: chapter, created_at. No money. The Q&A route is an explicit not_implemented stub.

extra.title: table: command_requests
extra.detail: Owner: nl_controller. chapter_id. RLS. Indexes: chapter, status, created_at. Direct update from commands service. Not a money table.

extra.title: table: event_types
extra.detail: Owner: events. chapter_id FK. RLS. Unique (chapter_id, lower(name)). No default_fine_amount column (that NUMERIC column is on event_templates; the stage-1 inventory is wrong). Direct insert from events service.

extra.title: table: event_groups
extra.detail: Owner: events. chapter_id. RLS. Index on chapter. Written with event create.

extra.title: table: event_organizers
extra.detail: Owner: events. Has chapter_id (index ix_event_organizers_chapter_id) despite the stage-1 inventory saying otherwise. RLS. FKs to events and members. Written by ev_add_organizer / ev_remove_organizer.

extra.title: table: event_audience_members
extra.detail: Owner: events. chapter_id indexed. RLS. Written by ev_set_audience. Indexes on chapter, event, member.

extra.title: table: task_commitments
extra.detail: Owner: tasks. chapter_id. RLS. Partial unique on one active commitment. Indexes: chapter, task, member. Written by tk_commit_task / tk_uncommit_task. fine_amount_cents if present is BIGINT, not the events NUMERIC column.

extra.title: table: task_commitment_log
extra.detail: Owner: tasks. chapter_id. RLS. Append-only trigger tk_block_commitment_log_mutation. Indexes: chapter, task, member, created_at. Written by the commit RPCs.

extra.title: table: invoice_line_items
extra.detail: Owner: treasury. chapter_id FK (inventory claim that it is missing is wrong). invoice_id FK CASCADE. CHECK amount > 0. Update and delete triggers. RLS select. Written inside tr_create_invoice_v2 when line items are passed. Sum must equal the invoice amount. Indexes: chapter, invoice.

extra.title: table: payment_evidence
extra.detail: Owner: treasury. chapter_id FK. submission_id FK. CHECK size 1..2MiB. Update and delete triggers. RLS select. Direct insert from payments.add_evidence, not an RPC. Indexes: chapter, submission.

extra.title: table: payment_allocations
extra.detail: Owner: treasury. chapter_id, verified_payment_id, invoice_id FKs, all ON DELETE CASCADE (the delete trigger makes the cascade fail). CHECK amount > 0. reverses_allocation_id self-FK. Update and delete triggers. RLS select. Written by tr_verify_payment_v2 and tr_reallocate_payment. Indexes: chapter, payment, invoice, partial reverses.

extra.title: table: announcement_sms_sends
extra.detail: Owner: announcements. chapter_id FK. RLS. Update guard an_enforce_sms_send_update. Unique lookup on (announcement, member) per the send RPC. Indexes on chapter, announcement, created_at. Written by an_send_announcement_sms.

extra.title: table: usage_events
extra.detail: Owner: instrumentation. chapter_id. RLS. Append-only trigger ux_block_usage_events_mutation. Indexes: chapter, (chapter, event_name), created_at. Direct insert from usage service.

extra.title: table: event_supervisors
extra.detail: Owner: events. chapter_id indexed. RLS. Written by ev_add_supervisor / ev_remove_supervisor. Indexes: chapter, event, member.

extra.title: table: event_notification_sends
extra.detail: Owner: events. chapter_id. RLS. Update guard ev_enforce_notify_send_update. Indexes: chapter, event. Dedup is in the notify RPC. Written by ev_notify_event.

extra.title: table: initiatives
extra.detail: Owner: initiatives. chapter_id. RLS. Index (chapter_id, date). Written by in_create_initiative / in_update_initiative.

extra.title: table: initiative_chairs
extra.detail: Owner: initiatives. chapter_id indexed (inventory 'no chapter_id' is wrong). RLS. Written by in_add_chair / in_remove_chair. Indexes: chapter, initiative, member.

extra.title: table: security_swap_requests
extra.detail: Owner: events. chapter_id. RLS. Partial unique on one pending swap. Update guard ev_enforce_swap_update. Indexes: chapter, event, target, requester. Written by ev_request/accept/decline/cancel security swap.

extra.title: table: member_setup_codes
extra.detail: Owner: auth. chapter_id FK. RLS select via rbac_request_chapter_id. Indexes: member, chapter. Direct insert from auth.py and from au_invite_member / au_consume_setup_code. code_hash only, not the raw code.

conventions.competing: Monolithic parallel batch load on app boot, Direct inline API client calls
conventions.dominant: On-demand domain hook data fetching with useEffect / refetch triggers
conventions.recommendation: Standardize on React Query or SWR for caching and refetching, rather than reinventing the wheel with monolithic boot loads.

conventions.competing: Client-only local state mutations generating synthetic IDs without API persistence, Async awaited API call with loading spinner and error handling
conventions.dominant: Optimistic React state updates with background API sync (no rollback on error)
conventions.recommendation: Use mutation hooks with explicit onSuccess/onError callbacks, ensuring optimistic state is fully rolled back via .catch() on error.

conventions.competing: Single composite object useState for form state
conventions.dominant: Multiple individual string/boolean useState variables per form input
conventions.recommendation: Adopt a form library (e.g., React Hook Form) or standardize on single composite objects to avoid useState bloat.

conventions.competing: Pure domain validation helper functions, Native HTML5 form input validation attributes
conventions.dominant: Inline onSubmit guard checks triggering showToast error notifications
conventions.recommendation: Move all validation to pure domain helpers returning typed { valid, error, body } objects (like planProof).

conventions.competing: Reusable ConfirmDialog, Standalone specialized full-screen overlay components
conventions.dominant: Generic reusable Modal component with backdrop, title, ESC key handling
conventions.recommendation: Consolidate into the reusable Modal component to ensure consistent ESC key and click-outside behaviors.

conventions.competing: Global useToast hook context singleton
conventions.dominant: Direct showToast invocation inside module components and domain hooks
conventions.recommendation: Maintain the global toast context but pass showToast directly from hooks to prevent context-drilling.

conventions.competing: Initial boot permission fetch storing Set<string>, localStorage token persistence
conventions.dominant: Pure session permission check utility functions (can, isOfficerView)
conventions.recommendation: Retain can() for fine-grained checks, but remove coarse isOfficerView logic to rely strictly on backend RBAC.

conventions.competing: Silent 403 error swallowing for optional officer endpoints via optionalOfficerCall, Custom error class hierarchy
conventions.dominant: Component-level try-catch block updating error string state or calling showToast
conventions.recommendation: Standardize error handling via an API client interceptor and consistent custom error classes; avoid swallowing 403s silently.

conventions.competing: Global app-level loading boolean in useBackend, Hook-scoped loading boolean state
conventions.dominant: Component-level submitting state disabling submit buttons and updating text
conventions.recommendation: Track isSubmitting locally per mutation to correctly disable specific buttons rather than locking the whole app.

conventions.competing: Complete data refetch re-querying entire backend endpoints on sync or action
conventions.dominant: In-memory React useState storage in useAppData without HTTP/query cache library
conventions.recommendation: Replace useAppData caching with a formal query client (React Query) to handle invalidation and caching correctly.

conventions.competing: Pure date formatting library functions avoiding UTC timezone shifts
conventions.dominant: Inline ISO string slicing in adapters.ts (day substring 0-10, hhmm substring 0-5)
conventions.recommendation: Enforce the use of pure date formatting library functions and eliminate all inline string slicing of ISO dates.

conventions.competing: Backend DTO TypeScript interfaces in api.ts, Frontend domain prototype interfaces in types.ts
conventions.dominant: Pure mapper functions in adapters.ts transforming DTOs into domain types
conventions.recommendation: Continue using pure mapper functions to shield domain components from backend snake_case DTOs.

conventions.competing: Coarse officer view check using isOfficerView(permissions), Legacy members.role string equality comparison
conventions.dominant: Fine-grained permission key check using can(permissions, key) with Set<string>
conventions.recommendation: Deprecate isOfficer and isOfficerView entirely in favor of explicit can(permissions, specific:key) checks.

conventions.competing: Client-side array filtering driven by tab selection or search input state
conventions.dominant: Standard HTML table elements with Tailwind CSS styling and inline item rendering
conventions.recommendation: Extract table components to reusable abstractions if pagination or sorting is required; otherwise standard HTML is fine.

conventions.competing: PageDto<T> generic interface defined in api.ts but unutilized
conventions.dominant: Full unpaginated list rendering of all array elements returned by backend API
conventions.recommendation: Implement actual API-driven pagination using the PageDto structure instead of client-side-only rendering of large arrays.
